title: Turning down Cab and Tommy Dorsey; Bud Freeman and Davey Tough say "get Jonah"
summary: Before joining Cab he had refused calls because he was with Stuff, and about 1938 Dorsey's trumpeter Bunny Berigan failed to show, so Bud Freeman and Davey Tough suggested Jonah (the story resumes after the tape change).

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: Oh, no. When he called me up the first time, I said, 'Oh, no, no.' I was playing with Stuff then, you know. I even turned Tommy Dorsey down, see. Once Tommy was there, about '38 there, when things was going. Bunny Berrigan was drunk, as we were talking, and he didn't show up, which he did sometimes. And so Bud Freeman and Davey Tough said, 'Well, get Jonah.'
